title: If It Had Not Happened: The Chaco War

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *si* + *hubiera* + participle, with *habría* + participle, from B1 Unit 35. It talks about a past that did not happen: *Si hubiera tenido más agua, habría resistido más*. In history it is good for thinking about conditions and consequences without saying what would certainly have happened. Use it for simple, close conditions.

sections.title: Past conditions that did not happen
rows: Si los soldados hubieran tenido más agua, habrían sufrido menos.
If the soldiers had had more water, they would have suffered less.
Si la guerra no hubiera terminado en 1935, habría muerto más gente.
If the war had not ended in 1935, more people would have died.
Si hubiéramos sabido la historia del Chaco, habríamos entendido el museo.
If we had known the history of the Chaco, we would have understood the museum.
Si el clima hubiera sido más fresco, las tropas habrían estado mejor.
If the climate had been cooler, the troops would have been better off.

items.spanish: Si hubieran tenido más agua, los soldados habrían sufrido menos en el Chaco.
items.english: If they had had more water, the soldiers would have suffered less in the Chaco.

items.spanish: Si la guerra hubiera continuado, habría habido más muertos.
items.english: If the war had continued, there would have been more dead.

items.spanish: Si no hubiera visto el museo, no habría entendido la historia.
items.english: If I had not seen the museum, I would not have understood the history.

sections.content: Never put *habría* after *si*: say *si hubiera tenido*, not *si habría tenido*. Both parts use *haber*: *hubiera* in the *si* clause and *habría* in the result. Keep the examples about conditions you can check, not about who would have won.
